content.text:
The report describes two failures. The first is a regime-dependent sign in V02: near-zero mean, unstable across regimes, negative in low-T and positive in high-T. The second is a slow-moving feature (rank autocorrelation 0.77) that was weakly negative and restricted to high-T. The report recommends testing an interaction with T and using faster-moving temporal features.

The proposed hypothesis uses different variables (V04 and V06) and a 12-month change, which is slow-moving. It expects positive IC in both T regimes, but it does not include any T interaction or any mechanism for handling regime-dependent signs. Twelve-month changes are typically highly autocorrelated, so the slowness failure is likely not avoided. The proposal also does not explicitly address either failure, because it is a new signal on different variables. It is a cross-sectional spread, which differs from the expanding-history standardization, but that is not explicitly a fix for either failure.

It does not explicitly avoid the failures. It even risks repeating the slow-moving problem and assumes regime consistency without testing.

{"avoids_failure": false}
